unharnessed.meaning: Every step and tip kept, quantities untouched; the vanilla-sugar swap is right ("swap two teaspoons of the white sugar for vanilla sugar"). "dark choc bits" and "like peanuts" are faithful localisations of semi-sweet morsels and groundnuts.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "plain flour", "bicarb soda", "baking paper", "marg", "wholemeal flour", "rolled oats", "not much chop to eat on its own", "Top-shelf butter".
unharnessed.authenticity: Reads like an Aussie recipe: "Chuck in the vanilla and beat it through", "bump up the spread", "make a cracker of a bikkie". Nothing stagey.
unharnessed.register: A clear level 3: localised terms throughout plus a conversational voice, without turning the recipe into a yarn. No swearing, fine at dad.
unharnessed.tone: Stays a helpful, practical recipe: "Let them sit for about 1 minute, then take them off the hot tray".
unharnessed.flow: Reads naturally: "Don't stack hot bikkies or they'll bend out of shape and won't cool as quick."
unharnessed.variety: Well varied; "bump the flour up" and "bump up the spread" and "cut down the spread" recur, but reasonably.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the original recipe with its notes and variations.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every point kept; "if it does stick, baking paper or non-stick trays can help" is a fair rewording; vanilla-sugar swap correct.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "plain flour", "bicarb soda", "marg", "not much chop", "beaut soft centre". "oatmeal" left, though rolled oats is the local term.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Mostly natural ("Leave them sit", "you mightn't like it", "won't spread out heaps"), with one clunky line, "gives a fair bit different taste".
yarn-dinkum.register: Level 3, a shade light: mostly plain recipe English with local terms ("Preheat the oven", "Add the vanilla extract and beat it in").
yarn-dinkum.flow: Mostly smooth; "gives a fair bit different taste from the" stumbles, and it alternates "bickies" and "biscuits" a lot.
yarn-dinkum.variety: Fair variety; "bickies" and "biscuits" alternate visibly, as in "thicker biscuits" then "thicker bickies".

engine.meaning: Content intact; text kept almost verbatim. "Spread them evenly on a baking tin" shifts pan to tin, trivially.
engine.sense: Swaps mostly fit ("plain flour", "bicarb soda", "baking paper"), but "bickie dough" and "chopped bar choccy" strain, and "Use cake flour instead of all-purpose" leaves the US term after "plain flour" in the list.
engine.authenticity: Mechanical word swaps in the original's formal prose produce mismatches: "a fairly stiff dough that will not spread out heaps", "Using chopped bar choccy instead of pre-formed chips will result in a more rustic texture".
engine.register: Mostly untranslated: "Add eggs one at a time, beating until fully incorporated", "The proportion of granulated to brown sugar may be adjusted to suit taste". Under level 3.
engine.flow: Clunky where slang meets formal syntax: "will not spread out heaps", "produce a superior biscuit" next to "choccy".
engine.variety: "bickies" and "choccy" swapped in mechanically wherever the words occur.

dinkum-3.meaning: All steps and tips kept; vanilla-sugar swap correct; "peanuts or whatever" loosens the example but keeps it optional; "every oven's a bit different" keeps cooking times may vary.
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "crank the oven", "Plonk the dough", "not much chop", "no matter how flash it is", "muck about with the mix", "rolled oats".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like an Aussie mate giving you the recipe: "baking paper or non-stick trays'll sort you out", "not stress about your bikkies going all puddly", "Bung in more vanilla extract".
dinkum-3.register: Level 3 leaning to 4: chattier than needed in places ("First up, crank the oven"), but stays a recipe. No swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Practical and friendly, as the original.
dinkum-3.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Don't go overboard beating it, or you'll get gluten forming".
dinkum-3.variety: Varied verbs and tags: "Chuck", "Plonk", "Bung", "Throw in", "Tip them", "muck about".

yarn-troppo.meaning: All steps kept; asides are colour ("believe it or not", "if you have a nibble of the chocolate on its own"). "puddles are the only reason anyone uses marg" garbles the logic (the reason is to avoid puddles).
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly fits ("not much chop", "flash", "top-shelf biscuit"), but "Go cake flour instead of plain" strains, "the gluten starts getting going" is muddled, and "groundnuts or whatever" keeps the non-local term.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural chat: "Don't go mad here", "Can't get hold of vanilla extract?", "bung them in the 350°F oven". A few forced lines.
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3, edging toward a chatty level 4 with asides added throughout.
yarn-troppo.tone: Still a helpful recipe; asides keep it friendly.
yarn-troppo.flow: Mostly smooth; "beat it too long and the gluten starts getting going" is clunky.
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied openers and verbs: "Crack the eggs in", "Tip in", "Chuck in", "bung them", "Go cake flour".

unharnessed.why: bump up and cut down used for spread several times; slight repetition.

yarn-dinkum.quote: gives a fair bit different taste from the
yarn-dinkum.original: will result in a significantly different taste than the
yarn-dinkum.why: Ungrammatical; a fair bit of a different taste or tastes a fair bit different.

yarn-dinkum.original: Add a small amount of oatmeal
yarn-dinkum.why: Rolled oats is what an Australian recipe would say.

engine.quote: a fairly stiff dough that will not spread out heaps
engine.original: a fairly stiff dough that will not spread out very much
engine.why: Slang dropped into formal syntax; an Australian would wince.

engine.quote: Using chopped bar choccy instead of pre-formed chips
engine.original: Using chopped bar chocolate instead of pre-formed chips
engine.why: Choccy forced into a technical phrase; block chocolate is the local term.

engine.quote: Use cake flour instead of all-purpose
engine.original: Use cake flour instead of all-purpose
engine.why: US term left even though the ingredients list says plain flour.

engine.quote: Stir in chocolate morsels (chips), and nuts if using.
engine.original: Stir in chocolate morsels (chips), and nuts if using.

dinkum-3.why: Or whatever is a touch loose for a recipe.

yarn-troppo.quote: and puddles are the only reason anyone uses marg in the first place
yarn-troppo.original: which is the only reason to use margarine in the first place
yarn-troppo.why: Says puddles are the reason, not avoiding them; muddled.

yarn-troppo.original: you may get some gluten formation

yarn-troppo.quote: Go cake flour instead of plain
yarn-troppo.original: Use cake flour instead of all-purpose

yarn-troppo.why: Groundnuts is not Australian; peanuts would be.

summaries.unharnessed: Natural, fully localised level-3 recipe that keeps every step and tip.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Faithful and natural, slightly light, with one clunky line.
summaries.engine: Rule-engine output: the original with term swaps, under the brief and clunky where slang meets formal prose.
summaries.dinkum-3: Lively, authentic, varied retelling; a shade chattier than level 3 but faithful throughout.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Varied and friendly, a bit heavier than asked, with a few muddled lines.
